decisions.reason: As a core safety-shoe line in the firm's main business, it likely stays because a large established manufacturer with ample production and logistics slack usually gives such launches more time unless results clearly disappoint.
A comfort insole is a close complement to the firm's footwear range, so even with only modest visibility the firm is likely to retain it while it learns about demand and cross-selling potential.
This supportive insole fits the firm's tailored-solution strategy, but because it may overlap with other insole offers its drop risk is a bit higher if early sales fall short of aspiration levels.
Its own dedicated page signals above-average organisational commitment, and an ergonomic safety-shoe series strongly matches the firm's innovation and workplace-health positioning.

Firefighter and rescue boots are a specialised adjacent category, yet the product remains likely to be kept because it leverages the firm's protective-footwear capabilities and large-firm resource slack.

Being shown on the home page suggests strong initial support, and a moulded insole is a low-distance extension of the core offer that the firm would usually continue unless performance is clearly unsatisfactory.
